geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant mass controller into a courtyard macro so the split-wing becomes a true public-void figure while preserving the existing bar ancestry.
Use a usable carved margin rather than a decorative subtraction.
Align the public opening to the verified access side in program frame.

graph_edits.rationale: Wrap the dominant split-wing mass with a clearer public void logic instead of leaving the frontage as a sealed split bar.
Open the split more so the interstice reads as a usable court or entry seam rather than a tight notch.
Introduce a ground-connected organizing element to strengthen the public threshold and make the split legible as neighborhood space.
Keep the spine slender so it anchors the composition without collapsing the open void.

rationale: The candidate reads as two blocky masses bridged by a narrow connector, but the overall composition is still too generic and under-articulated for the neighborhood-living brief. In the four views it is only modestly coherent: the isometric and front views suggest a split-wing datum, yet the top view shows an awkward pinch rather than a clearly public court or a robust threshold. The blue frontage edge is not answered by a legible open ground condition; the street response feels mostly sealed and semantically indifferent. The silhouette is not a capacity-bearing step form, but a basic bar split into chunks, so it does not deliver the required active ground/public void relationship. Repair integrity is acceptable because the mass remains manifold and not visibly self-colliding, but the program relation is weak: it looks closer to an abstract split bar than a compact mixed-use building with an active edge and useful void. A stronger correction would be to preserve the dominant split-wing gesture while carving a clearer court or notch aligned to the access edge, or to introduce a more explicit sectional/terraced roof family only if it still protects the ground threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a community-center/campus-like complex, so its spread and public court logic transfer better than its institutional scale or roof mix.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise, multi-wing composition organized around a legible shared void and terrace/circulation figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Very small hospitality pavilion; useful as an access/entry precedent, but not as a model for the candidate's larger mass hierarchy.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple pavilion mass with a clear ground threshold and a small vertical/service accent can support a neighborhood-facing edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual housing precedent; its strong sectional ribbon is more intense than needed here, but the public-void and stepped-hierarchy principle is transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Sectional terrace/ramp logic and a courtyard-like void can preserve neighborhood life while varying the upper mass.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the shown views; no hard gate rejection on boundary fit.
The access edge response is weak: no clearly legible public void, entry seam, or undercut along the blue frontage.
Form coherence is limited; the object is readable mostly as a simple split bar rather than a fuller neighborhood-building section.
Do not copy the 8 House reference literally; only the sectional public-void principle is transferable.
